view.title: Paid Social Strategy
view.dek: A look at the creative approaches brands use in their Meta ads, who they speak to and how they encourage action.
view.scope: Meta Ad Library, Canada, active ads only. A one-day snapshot, collected 30 October 2026 at 5:28 p.m. Toronto time.
view.limits: For these ads in Canada the library shows no spend, impressions or reach, so this describes what each brand runs, not how well it performs. Ad text was read in full; videos and images were not reviewed frame by frame.

messages.message: Switch from a big bank to a faster, cheaper business account
messages.offers: 2% interest; 1% cashback described as “unlimited” and “no caps, no minimums”; 0.25% FX against “3%+ at the Big Banks”; 15,000+ businesses
messages.conditions: No terms or conditions in the text of any of the 20 ads

messages.message: Less finance busywork, with cards, bills and expenses in one platform
messages.offers: “Up to 3.75% interest”; “Best Canadian Corporate Cards”; a comparison with American Express
messages.conditions: No terms or conditions in the text of any of the 11 ads

messages.message: Control spending and automate finance work, told industry by industry
messages.offers: 1% cash back “now available in Canada”; no FX fees on CAD and USD; 70,000+ customers; a $60 billion valuation
messages.conditions: Ads for the Canadian card add “Terms and conditions apply” and a Peoples Trust card disclosure; 8 of 47 carry US bank disclosures instead

messages.message: Banking for Canadian businesses that buy and sell across borders
messages.offers: 0% FX on card spend from four currencies; $0 wire fees; “Save $40K+/year”; a worked example of a 3% bank margin
messages.conditions: One ad names its source (Bank of Canada research) for bank margins; the $40K figure shows no basis in the ad

messages.message: No active ads in Canada when collected
Pay, hold and spend money across countries
messages.offers: Pay in 60+ currencies; 0% FX fees; cards for 60+ markets; 675,000+ businesses
messages.conditions: No terms or conditions in the text of any of the 24 ads

examples.title: A rewards claim with no cap in the ad
examples.observed: The ad promises “1% cashback” alongside “Zero hidden fees” and lists cards, FX and transfers. Other Venn ads in the set say “no caps, no minimums”.
examples.reading: The ad states the rate without the plan limit that Venn’s pricing footnote set on 23 October.
examples.limits: The footnote was not rechecked on 30 October, so whether the limit still applies is not established. The video was not watched.

examples.title: One message per industry, each with its own page
examples.observed: 25 of Ramp’s 47 ads point to industry pages: 12 for nonprofits, 8 for healthcare and 5 for construction, each written to that reader (“Grant compliance is not a game of chance.”).
examples.reading: The ads and the pages they open speak to one kind of business at a time, so the first screen after the click can stay on the same problem.
examples.limits: The landing pages were not reviewed. Which audiences saw each ad is not shown in the library.

examples.title: A worked example with a named source
examples.observed: One ad works through a payment: “On a US$50,000 payment, a 3% bank margin costs about US$1,500”, and names Bank of Canada research for the margin. Another ad says “Save $40K+/year” with no basis shown.
examples.reading: The worked example gives a reader something to check; the round savings figure asks them to trust it.
examples.limits: The cited research and the arithmetic were not checked here.

examples.title: Comparison pages as the destination
examples.observed: One Airwallex ad sends people to an “Airwallex vs Ramp” comparison page, and one Float ad promotes an “American Express vs. Float” comparison.
examples.reading: Both meet a buyer who is already weighing options, at the point of comparing.
examples.limits: The comparison pages themselves were not reviewed for accuracy.

website_check.ads: “Get 1% cash back with our corporate card, now available in Canada” and “1% back on CAD and USD, no FX fees”
website_check.web: A Canadian rewards rate was not found in the reviewed sources (23 October).
The pricing footnote limited eligible card spend on Essentials and Plus (23 October).
Account interest of 2.5%, up to 3.5% in a promotion (23 October).
The homepage gave 200,000 and 600,000+ businesses (23 October).

website_check_note: These ads are dated 30 October and the website evidence 23 October, so a difference may be a change over the week rather than a contradiction. None of them changes the findings or counts in this case study; each is listed for editorial review.
ramp_note: The Ramp Facebook page in the library sends its ads to ramp.com, and 3 of its ads thank @tryramp for “Tony Stock” content. That is new evidence on the unresolved @tryramp question in Social Media Strategy, kept for editorial review; the Instagram analysis still treats @tryramp as unresolved.
counts_note: The library’s count for each page and the records returned can differ: for Venn the library reported 34 active ads and 20 records came back, each record grouping one or more versions (43 versions in all). Totals here use the records returned.

suggests.observed: None of Venn’s, Float’s or Airwallex’s ad text mentions terms or conditions, including beside reward, interest and FX-fee claims.
suggests.reading: An ad is often the first place a buyer meets the offer. Without the condition there, the website has to correct the impression later.
suggests.test: Add the main condition to the ad text or the first screen the ad opens, and compare qualified sign-ups per click (see test 1 in Lessons).

suggests.observed: 25 of Ramp’s 47 ads send people to pages for one industry: nonprofits, healthcare or construction.
suggests.reading: Matching the ad and the page to one kind of business keeps the message consistent after the click.
suggests.test: For your largest audience, compare a matched landing page with a general one on qualified sign-ups per click, using your own analytics.

suggests.observed: 102 of the 119 ads started in the 30 days before collection; one Loop ad had run since June and two Venn ads since July.
suggests.reading: A one-day snapshot shows what runs now, not a long-term strategy. Running a long time does not prove an ad works.
suggests.test: Repeat the collection monthly and track which messages keep running alongside your own results.

Ramp: 23 of 35 name an industry, such as nonprofits, healthcare or construction.
Loop: 13 of 14 are about international payments.
Airwallex: 19 of 21 are text-led graphics, and all 21 are product-focused.
Float: a small sample; 5 of 5 reviewed creatives are about reducing finance admin.

method: Snapshot: the Meta Ad Library, Canada, active ads, collected 30 October 2026 at 5:28 p.m. Toronto time (119 ad records). The creative files were read from the same collection on 31 October 2026; no ads were added or swapped.

Every image was inspected. Every video was reviewed as frames sampled evenly across its whole length (8 to 24 frames), with on-screen captions read; audio was not heard, so spoken words count only where they appear on screen.
Dynamic ads list several alternative creatives; each was reviewed as its own asset. No ad in the snapshot was a carousel.

Unit of analysis: a distinct creative execution within a brand. The 119 ads held 288 media slots and 196 distinct files; byte-identical files count once, and near-identical files (matching image or middle frame, same brand, type and length within 1.5 seconds) count once, leaving 175 assets. A resize, crop or re-cut with the same hook, message and visual story counts once (88 such links), leaving 87 distinct creatives; a different hook, message, visual story or format counts as a new creative.

Percentage = creatives in the category divided by the brand's distinct creatives, times 100, rounded to a whole number. Bar widths use the unrounded values. Focus, format and buying stage have one label each and add up to 100% before rounding. Creative approach, theme and persona can have several labels, so they are not forced to 100%.

Labels describe what the creative shows and says. Personas and buying stages are inferred from the content, not from Meta targeting, objectives or results; the library shows no spend, impressions or reach for these ads.
Ad record counts, Meta's displayed library counts, exact file variants and distinct creatives are different numbers; this section counts distinct creatives only.
